text: After this you can identify the actions needed to organize a support decision study.

For education only; this is not legal, purchasing, financial or safety advice. Stage A creates a common plan for the review. Define the trigger, intended decision, scope, roles, data needs, schedule and material risks. Include users, technical specialists, delivery owners and reviewers as relevant. Assign unresolved questions to a named role and a next action. Agreement on a plan is not the same as authorization to make binding commitments.

items: Confirm the reason for the study and the decision expected. You should see: The team shares a clear mandate. If not: Escalate uncertainty over scope or authority.
Assign participants, deliverables and dates. You should see: Every major work item has an owner and schedule. If not: Identify missing expertise or resources.
Document assumptions, risks and open questions. You should see: Follow-up work is visible and assigned. If not: Give unresolved matters an owner and next review date.
Inferred: A review starts with a one-page statement of its goal, boundaries, decision owner, evidence gaps and the next check-in.

text: Obtain a shared mandate and clear ownership of tasks.
Significant new evidence may require the original plan to be revised.
